places.ad: Potong Pasir Avenue 1 / Avenue 2 (Blk 101-142), Singapore
places.w: Completed 1984, these steep red-pitched roofs are Singapore's most visually distinctive HDB silhouette — a mid-1980s experiment in postmodern public housing that borrowed the Malay kampong-house form to break from the usual slab blocks. Top-floor units get soaring 5-5.5 m ceilings, and Block 142's 'welcome' sign has become the emblem of the whole estate.
places.k: Public estate; view from ground level

places.ad: 11 Bidadari Park Drive (opposite Woodleigh MRT), Singapore
places.w: A 13-hectare urban park opened 3 September 2024 on the former Bidadari burial grounds, centred on Alkaff Lake — a stormwater-retention pond inspired by the colonial-era Alkaff Lake Gardens — with a 700 m Heritage Walk. Developed jointly by HDB, NParks, PUB and the National Heritage Board as the green heart of the new Bidadari estate.

places.ad: 66 Pheng Geck Avenue, Singapore 348261
places.w: Built in 1932 by Syed Abdul Rahman Alkaff of the prominent Hadhrami-Arab merchant family, this small mosque on the Potong Pasir/Bidadari edge is distinguished by a pencil-thin Ottoman-style minaret unlike any other in Singapore. Restored in 2014 and gazetted the same year as Singapore's 68th National Monument.

places.ad: 15 Francis Thomas Drive, Singapore 359342
places.w: A 13.5-hectare Anglican mission-school complex opened in 2006, straddling the Kallang River on the Potong Pasir/Woodsville banks and linking St Andrew's Junior, Secondary and Junior College — descendants of the St Andrew's Church Mission School founded in 1862 — across the Jacob Ballas Bridge.

places.n: Lorong Koo Chye Sheng Hong Temple
places.ad: 15 Arumugam Road, Singapore 409960
places.w: A prominent Taoist temple near MacPherson MRT dedicated to the City God (Cheng Huang Ye), the Sheng Hong deity whose spirit was brought from Anxi, China. Rooted in the old Kampong Koo Chye, it relocated to Arumugam Road in the 1980s when the area was redeveloped for industry and is now a large temple-and-charity association drawing crowds for prosperity and good-fortune prayers.

places.ad: 91 Kallang Road, Singapore 208804
places.w: A Hindu temple to Shiva (as Manmatha Karuneshvarar) established in 1888 on the Potong Pasir/Kallang edge, begun by Hindu workers of the nearby colonial gasworks who installed the deity for protection — hence its nickname the 'Kallang Gasworks Sivan Temple'. Rebuilt in 1934 on a 1909 government land grant.

places.ad: Jalan Wangi / Sennett Road (bounded by Upper Serangoon Rd & MacPherson Rd), Singapore
places.w: Once dubbed Singapore's largest planned housing development, Sennett Estate was built out through the 1950s (completed 1955) by the Sennett Realty and Tan Chong Land companies on land that had been Alkaff's leisure garden in the 1920s. Today a quiet, leafy middle-class landed enclave of terraces and bungalows ringed by the Potong Pasir and MacPherson HDB towns.

places.ad: Bidadari Park (eastern section), Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore
places.w: From 1907-1972 the Bidadari grounds were Singapore's main multi-faith cemetery — Christian, Muslim, Hindu and Sinhalese — resting place of luminaries like Lim Boon Keng. After exhumation (2001-2006) of tens of thousands of graves, its history is preserved in a memorial garden and heritage relics folded into today's Bidadari Park, an estate reborn as 'a community in a garden'.

places.ad: 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
places.w: The civic heart of the new Bidadari estate: a three-storey mall opened May 2023 (officially November 2023) integrated with the Bidadari Community Club, a neighbourhood police centre, the Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre and Woodleigh MRT — nature-inspired gathering spaces knit into the adjacent Bidadari Park and Alkaff Lake.

places.ad: Kallang Park Connector (through Potong Pasir), Singapore
places.w: Potong Pasir means 'cut sand' in Malay — from 1910-1937 the area was sand quarries whose worked-out pits became ponds linked to the Kallang River. The river still threads the estate, and the Bidadari/Kallang Park Connector now runs alongside it, joining Potong Pasir to Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and down to the Kallang basin.

places.ad: MacPherson Road (Aljunied to Paya Lebar), Singapore
places.w: MacPherson takes its name from Colonel Ronald MacPherson, the Straits Settlements' first Colonial Secretary; MacPherson Road itself was once Jalan Klapa, running through coconut plantations. The estate's first eleven 10-storey blocks went up in 1961, an early chapter of Singapore high-rise housing, beside the Circuit Road town and the Tai Seng/Paya Lebar industrial belt.

places.ad: Potong Pasir Avenue 1, Singapore
places.w: One of the rare central estates with no mega-mall or high-rise sprawl, Potong Pasir keeps a laid-back, almost kampong-spirited feel between Toa Payoh and Sennett. The sign-crowned Block 142 at the foot of the sloping-roof blocks is its unofficial gateway and most-photographed civic landmark.
places.k: Public estate; view from ground level

places.ad: Former palace site, Bidadari estate (off Upper Serangoon Road / Mount Vernon Road), Singapore
places.w: The estate and the whole Bidadari district take their name from this vanished palace. British engineer Henry Minchin Simons acquired the 45-acre grounds in 1855; Sultan Abu Bakar of Johor bought it in the 1860s and gifted it to his second wife, the Danish-born Sultana Zubaidah (Cecilia Catharina Lange) — its beauty likened to a 'bidadari' (Malay/Sanskrit for celestial nymph or angel). After Zubaidah moved to Johor the palace was rented out, then demolished in 1915; its name outlived it, passing to the cemetery and today's estate.

places.ad: 8 Potong Pasir Avenue 2, Singapore 358362
places.w: A Hindu temple to Shiva and the goddess Durga, first erected in 1906 near the Lavender Street / Rumah Miskin junction and shifted three times — via Beatty Road — before settling in Potong Pasir in 1982. Demolished in 2014 for water-leakage and space problems and rebuilt in Dravidian style at a cost of S$2.7 million, it was reconsecrated on 4 December 2016, with chambers for Ganesha, Murugan, Shiva, Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswati.

places.ad: Former garden site, Bidadari (Woodleigh / Upper Aljunied vicinity), Singapore
places.w: The green ancestor of today's Alkaff Lake: from 1929/30 to 1964 the wealthy Hadhrami-Arab Alkaff family ran a magnificent Japanese-style pleasure garden east of the Bidadari Cemetery — artificial hills, tea houses and a large ornamental lake landscaped with Japanese help. It closed and was cleared in the 1960s (the site now around Cedar Girls' Secondary), but its memory is deliberately echoed by the Alkaff Lake completed in Bidadari Park in 2024.

places.ad: 77 Circuit Road, #01-450, MacPherson, Singapore 370077
places.w: Young hawkerpreneur Douglas Ng rebuilt his grandmother's recipe into a hawker-fame story — soft, bouncy fishballs made from pure yellowtail with no added flour that won a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2016; after stints at Golden Mile and Timbre+, the stall settled at Blk 77 Circuit Road in MacPherson.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-29, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
places.w: Opened by former local actor Huang Yiliang, this humble evening-only stall cooks each bowl of crab bee hoon to order, drawing out a deeply sweet seafood broth — with a steamed fish and homemade omelette that regulars rate just as highly. A cult name of the renovated Circuit Road hawker centre.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-10, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
places.w: An old-school Hokkien mee (from S$4) simmered and fried in prawn-head and pork stock with egg, prawn, pork and yellow noodles, then left to stew so the strands soak up the umami — a repeatedly-listed Circuit Road favourite the food blogs queue for.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-92, 79A Circuit Road, Singapore 371079
places.w: Victor's vegetarian satay — grilled mock-meat skewers at around S$1 a stick — draws long lines from residents and non-vegetarians alike, alongside otah and a spread of meat-free hawker classics that regularly headline Circuit Road stall guides.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-19, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: The uncle who dances to instrumental music as he fries — his char kway teow is cooked with less oil than most and can be topped with a soft-boiled egg or omelette (about S$5), a Circuit Road performance-and-plate that the SPH food titles keep naming.

places.ad: 538 MacPherson Road, Singapore 368222
places.w: A family-run 24-hour Indian-Muslim diner on MacPherson Road since 1998 and a go-to supper spot — famed for prata that comes out crispy on the outside yet slightly doughy within, plus a well-loved mutton nasi biryani (~S$7) and proper mutton soup for the night-shift crowd.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A claypot specialist whose range runs from smoked-duck rice and barbecue-pork rice to pig trotters and bak kut teh, with a classic claypot chicken rice around S$7 — a hearty Circuit Road standby featured across the SPH stall round-ups.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-14, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A family-run briyani stall with a deliberately tiny menu — just chicken briyani and mutton briyani, both under S$7 — plating generous, flavourful helpings that make it one of the Circuit Road names the food titles single out.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A third-generation hawker cooking fried oyster, orh luak (oyster omelette) and fried carrot cake from a family recipe handed down by his grandfather — an old-school Circuit Road wok stall the SPH lifestyle titles both flag.

places.ad: 1 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347834
places.w: A Potong Pasir prawn-noodle institution first established in 1971 and now second-generation, named for the ancestral province of founder Png Kim Soon. The broth is built from fried prawn shells and pork ribs simmered eight hours, served across a sprawling 20-dish menu of prawn, pork rib, intestine, baby abalone and clam combinations.

places.ad: Sin Keng Seng Eating House, 47 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347867
places.w: Opened by an apprentice of a famous bak chor mee master, this Tai Thong Crescent coffeeshop stall turns out an old-school minced-pork noodle — vinegary, lard-slicked, with fresh pork liver — that veteran hawker bloggers rank among the area's best.

places.ad: The Commerze @ Irving, 1 Irving Place, Singapore 369546
places.w: An ex-Hyatt manager's stall cooking authentic Seremban, Malaysia dishes — springy cuttlefish bee hoon (lai fen) with sweet sauce and a rich pork curry. After its beloved hole-in-the-wall Potong Pasir Ave 3 coffeeshop closed in March 2024, it reopened bigger and air-conditioned at The Commerze @ Irving in Sept 2024, on the MacPherson/Tai Seng edge.

places.ad: 148 Potong Pasir Avenue 1, #01-37, Singapore 350148
places.w: Run by the third generation behind the old Shangri-La Confectionery & Delicatessen, Kizuna is the family's Potong Pasir revamp from heritage bakery into a neighbourhood cafe — keeping the old-school bakes while adding brunch plates and coffee.

places.ad: 51 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-59 Poiz Centre, Singapore 347697
places.w: A vibrant salmon-pink cafe tucked into Poiz Centre, known for crisp brown-butter waffles, cakes and gelato and inventive drinks (Grape Yakult Honey Sencha) — Eatbook scored it 7.5/10 and it's become a study-and-brunch favourite of the estate.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-30, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: ITE culinary grads Darryl and Shi Long bring affordable European dining to a hawker stall — their best-selling duck confit (S$12) is a fork-tender leg on fluffy mash in a moat of rich house sauce, plus truffle pasta — a headline act of the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A legendary kway chap name dating to the 1980s, now with a Woodleigh Village outlet — a set from S$5 gets broad rice sheets in braised gravy with expertly done pork belly, big and small intestine, tau pok and more.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-27, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A rare Henghua (Putian)-style white lor mee — a velvety, savoury (not dark) broth loaded with seafood, pork and vegetables — one of the standout regional-Chinese stalls the food guides pick out at Woodleigh Village.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-18, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: An outlet of the famed fried-chicken-wing name some rate the best in Singapore — light, crackly skin over juicy meat — one of the established brands that anchored the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre when it opened in Sept 2024.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-13, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: The hawker centre's sole vegetarian stall, run by Darryl Tong, plating a menu that reads nothing like a typical meat-free spread — 'char siew' kolo mee, fried fish bee hoon and kway chap done entirely vegan.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: Fragrant Kelantanese-style nasi kerabu — gorgeous blue-pea rice (S$7.80) with herbs and a crisp, juicy fried chicken leg — one of the young-hawker Malay stalls the food guides highlight at Woodleigh Village.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-35, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A specialist in authentic Cantonese porridge — silky, slow-simmered congee — among the quieter but well-regarded stalls the food bloggers pick out at the new Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A Mexican stall bringing hearty rice bowls and tacos to hawker prices — part of the wave of young, cross-cuisine entrepreneurs that made Woodleigh Village one of Singapore's most internationally varied hawker centres.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-40, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: Crisp-shelled HK-style egglets (gai daan jai) served as ice-cream sandwiches and waffles — the sweet-treat stall that both major food guides call out by name at Woodleigh Village.

places.ad: The Woodleigh Mall, #01-55, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
places.w: A cosy Bidadari cafe from the team of a Singapore National Barista Champion — carefully pulled specialty coffee alongside cafe fare like avocado toast and shakshuka, a draw for the estate's brunch crowd.

places.ad: The Woodleigh Mall, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
places.w: A train-themed, pet-friendly outpost of the Australian grocer-cafe, with a cabin-style seating nook and signature pancake stacks (the Fried Chicken Stack pairs Pancake Parlour pancakes with buttermilk fried chicken and chilli honey) — a headline brunch anchor of the Bidadari mall.

places.ad: 80 Circuit Road, #02-10, Block 80 Market & Food Centre, Singapore 370080
places.w: One of the last hawker stalls in Singapore still selling noodles from S$2.50 — old-school bak chor mee and fishball noodles tossed in chilli-and-mushroom sauce with handmade wontons. The senior couple, at Circuit Road since 2006 (the name comes from stall no.10 at NUS Engineering's canteen), keep the price down for the neighbourhood's elderly; Mothership profiled their refusal to raise it.

places.n: Yong Lai Fa Ji Shu Shi
places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-66, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A Circuit Road fish-soup stall rated by veteran bloggers as on par with the famous Amoy Street bowl — fresh, bouncy fish in a robust broth simmered from fish bones and chicken for at least eight hours, with the fried sole-fish (ti poh) and ikan bilis made in-house. Fish soup around S$4.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-54, 79 Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A hidden-gem halal Thai beef-noodle stall at Circuit Road — the signature bowl (S$6) piles three forms of beef over kangkong and bean sprouts in a light, clear yet beefy broth (free refills) simmered at least three hours, fragrant with cloves and fried garlic. Reviewed by all three of the major SG food titles.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, #01-07, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A single-dish lor mee stall that has sustained itself since the 1970s on one bowl done well — a strong, savoury, gently vinegary gravy with crispy fried yam and plain hard-boiled egg, the thick starchy sauce slurpable to the last. From S$3, with a bigger S$5 portion; the boss is famously courteous.

places.n: Hup Hup Mee Siam・Laksa・Lor Mee
places.ad: Block 80 Circuit Road Market & Food Centre (Level 2), 80 Circuit Road, Singapore 370080
places.w: Second-generation hawker Joseph's Circuit Road stall, named a Top 10 Mee Siam in Singapore by Shin Min Daily News — a peanut-rich, addictively sour-and-light gravy (S$3). The laksa and an 'converted me into a lor mee lover' lor mee (S$4-5, packed with tau pok, hum and fish cake) round out the trio.

places.ad: Circuit Road Market & Food Centre, 79/79A Circuit Road, Singapore 370079
places.w: A Cantonese roast-meats stall at Circuit Road turning out char siew rice (from S$4) and roasted-pork noodles (S$4.50) alongside its roast duck — a value roast-meats standby both SPH lifestyle titles single out in their Circuit Road round-ups.

places.ad: The Poiz Centre, 51 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 347697
places.w: Young owner Shan Chew's under-the-radar Potong Pasir sandwich cafe, drawing foodies island-wide for a tight menu of hefty sandwiches (the Breakfast Sandwich with candied bacon; a juicy Wagyu patty melt), sourdough and sustainable specialty coffee — with pizzas after 6pm. A Time Out and Eatbook favourite of the estate.

places.ad: 83 MacPherson Lane, Singapore 360083
places.w: A value-for-money zi char stall in a MacPherson Lane coffeeshop that went viral for restaurant-grade shellfish at hawker prices — crab claws at S$5 each (four kam-heong claws for S$20), salted-egg crab around S$30 — and, unexpectedly, one of the better Penang-style char kway teow around, which is what drew ieatishootipost.

places.n: Yi Jia South Village Seafood Restaurant
places.ad: 544 MacPherson Road, Singapore 368225
places.w: A zi char that grew from a Toa Payoh coffeeshop into a full seafood restaurant on MacPherson Road, famed for its signature honeydew prawns — wild-caught ang kah prawns in a secret honeydew-melon sauce, served inside the melon itself — plus salted-egg crab and curry fish head. A long-running favourite of the veteran hawker bloggers.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: Young hawkerpreneur Xiao Xuan and her mother's donburi stall (started 2022 at Bukit Canberra) brings Japanese rice bowls under S$10 to Woodleigh Village — a Caramelised Char Siew Don (S$7) of smoky-sweet pork belly with a sous-vide egg, plus mentaiko chicken katsu and Angus sukiyaki dons.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A wholesome, budget-friendly wanton mee at Woodleigh Village — springy egg noodles with char siew, wontons and sides of ngoh hiang and chicken cutlet — repeatedly named among the centre's best-value stalls across the SethLui, Daniel Food Diary and Eatbook guides.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-11, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: Young hawker Nam's halal-certified fried-rice specialist at Woodleigh Village, plating several styles — Egg Fried Rice (S$3.20), sambal, curry and hae bee hiam — from a stall HungryGoWhere featured in its 'Hawker Hustlers' series. One of the young-entrepreneur stalls that defined the new centre.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-28, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: The Woodleigh outlet of the well-followed Whampoa Nan Xiang chicken rice, helmed by the owner's son Shaun — silky, tender steamed or roasted chicken with fragrant rice, portions from S$4.50, popular for its value sets.

places.ad: Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre, #01-31, 202C Woodleigh Link, Singapore 360202
places.w: A young-hawker stall billed as serving Singapore's first white curry prawn noodles — a milder, creamy take on curry laksa built on a prawn base — one of the cross-cuisine newcomers Eatbook picked out among Woodleigh Village's young hawkers.

places.ad: 45 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore
places.w: A Seoul-cool industrial cafe that opened in Potong Pasir in Feb 2024 — grey tones, plants and raw walls — but serving affordable kopitiam fare: Traditional Kaya Toast (S$2.60) with cold-butter slabs and silky kaya, plus nasi lemak, mee siam and mee rebus, with kopi till midnight. Reviewed by Eatbook, SethLui and Daniel Food Diary.

places.ad: 37 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347862
places.w: Started by three SMU graduates with an Italy-trained chef, this Sennett-edge gelato joint handcrafts fresh flavours daily — Honey Chrysanthemum with cacao nibs, hazelnut, biscoff, marshmallow oreo — served with a crisp-yet-fluffy waffle. Open late; reviewed by Daniel Food Diary, ladyironchef and Entree Kibbles.

places.ad: 120 Potong Pasir Avenue 1, #01-820, Singapore 350120
places.w: Chef Ivy Ling's cosy heartland cafe-patisserie tucked under a Potong Pasir HDB block, plating artisan bakes and cafe fare — a neighbourhood spot HungryGoWhere and Daniel Food Diary both flagged as a new Potong Pasir opening.

places.ad: The Venue Shoppes, 2 Tai Thong Crescent, Singapore 347836
places.w: A vegetarian zi char at The Venue Shoppes plating meat-free, wok-hei versions of Singaporean hawker classics — vegetarian char kway teow and fried Hokkien noodles (S$6.80 each), with no-egg options — the chef's wok skill carrying the dish without meat or seafood.

places.ad: The Poiz Centre, 51 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-12/13, Singapore 347697
places.w: A hidden Japanese convenience store and cafe by Potong Pasir MRT — a legit konbini stocking Japanese cup noodles (clam chowder, curry udon, Sapporo shrimp miso) alongside a cook-to-order cafe of crispy chicken karaage, oden and potato croquettes (from S$2.50) with fillings like sweet potato, chestnut and cheese.

places.ad: The Woodleigh Mall, 11 Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore 367803
places.w: The Woodleigh Mall outlet of the popular Malaysian beancurd chain, best known for silky tau fu fah (beancurd pudding) piled with toppings, plus Taiwanese-style shaved ice with grass jelly and aiyu — a dessert anchor of the Bidadari mall flagged by Eatbook and HungryGoWhere.
